title: Fixed-arity operation spaces of the groupoid string-to-pair map
statement:
Use the universe, space and infinity-category conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], the coherent nerves and string/operator categories of [lem-coef-simplicial-operator-nerve], and the multicategory $O_G$ and functor $\Phi_G$ with their explicit formulas of [lem-coef-operad-groupoid-operator-map]. Let $G$ be any small fibrant simplicial groupoid and set $X=N_{\mathrm{hc}}G$, $M=N_{\mathrm{hc}}D(G)$, $O=N_{\mathrm{hc}}O_G^\otimes$ and $f=N_{\mathrm{hc}}\Phi_G$. For objects $x,y$ of $G$ and $n\geq0$, let $\operatorname{Op}_{M,n}(x,y)$ be the space of active arrows from objects of $M_{[n]}$ to $(x,y)\in M_{[1]}$, with coherent triangles whose source-change edges are equivalences over the identity of $[n]$, retaining all higher simplices. Define $\operatorname{Op}_{O,n}(x,y)$ in the same manner. These are the arity-$n$ parts of the operation spaces in [lem-coef-operadic-localization-operation-criterion].

Let $A_x$ be the space of arrows of $X$ starting at $x$, allowing the final endpoint to vary, and $B_y$ the space of arrows ending at $y$, allowing the initial endpoint to vary; morphisms and higher simplices are coherent triangles and homotopies with the specified endpoint fixed. For every $n\geq1$ there are equivalences of spaces
$$\operatorname{Op}_{M,n}(x,y)\simeq A_x\times X^{n-1}\times B_y,\qquad
\operatorname{Op}_{O,n}(x,y)\simeq A_x\times\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,X)^{n-1}\times B_y.$$
They identify the map induced by $f$ with the identity on $A_x,B_y$ and the constant-path map on every internal factor. The endpoint convention on the first factor for $M$ is changed by inversion. Thus this induced map is an equivalence for every $n\geq1$.

For $n=0$, both operation spaces are equivalent to $\operatorname{Map}_X(x,y)$ and $f$ induces an equivalence. Under these identifications a source object $(z,a:z\to x,b:z\to y)$ on the $M$ side maps to $ba^{-1}$; an inverse on the path-space description sends $h:x\to y$ to $(x,1_x,h)$. All assertions are about the full coherent operation spaces, not only components, and use only identity-arity source changes.

proof.text: First fix the arity. By [lem-coef-operadic-localization-operation-criterion] source changes must lie over the identity of $[n]$. Thus the operation space is the pullback of the target-fixed arrow slice along the source fiber, followed by restriction to the component of the unique active map $[n]\to[1]$. By [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration] this is a right fibration over that source fiber, with fibers the corresponding active mapping spaces. Pullback and restriction to the specified discrete base-map component preserve the horn-lifting property: the missing triangle is filled in the original slice and its base map is forced. By [lem-coef-simplicial-operator-nerve], the source fiber for $M$ is $X^{n+1}$. For $O$ its displayed operator mapping formula over the identity of $[n]$ is the product of the unary mapping sets, hence its source fiber is $(X^{\mathrm{op}}\times X)^n$ by the unary formula in [lem-coef-operad-groupoid-operator-map]. All these fibers are spaces: unary arrows are invertible and $G$ is locally Kan, so [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] applies. The dual classification in [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] identifies each operation space with the total space of its active-mapping-space functor, contravariant in the source. Its transport is precomposition. This keeps the coherent triangles and every higher simplex, rather than quotienting their vertices.

proof.text: Let $n\geq1$. For a string $(z_0,\ldots,z_n)$ the active mapping space to $(x,y)$ is $G(z_0,x)\times G(z_n,y)$: the opposite active map selects precisely the two endpoints. This is the string mapping formula of [lem-coef-simplicial-operator-nerve]. A source change $(u_0,\ldots,u_n)$ acts by precomposition at those two endpoints and does nothing in the internal coordinates. Invert the first arrow, writing the operation as $(\alpha:x\to z_0,z_1,\ldots,z_{n-1},\gamma:z_n\to y)$. Strict inverses commute with every simplicial operator by [lem-coef-operad-groupoid-operator-map], and [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] respects composition coherently. Under [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], the endpoint functors have total spaces $A_x$ and $B_y$ (the source-fixed and target-fixed arrow spaces); each unused internal coordinate has total space $X$. Taking their product gives $A_x\times X^{n-1}\times B_y$. Indeed both sides classify the same product mapping-space functor: a simplex in the product over a source simplex is exactly a tuple of endpoint simplices, with independent internal coordinates. Uniqueness under transport classification gives the required equivalence for $M$.

proof.text: To recognize the internal factors on the $O$ side, the two-endpoint evaluation $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,X)\to X\times X$ is a Kan fibration: apply [lem-cbc-internal-hom-fibration-corner-map] to $\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ and $X\to *$, using that $X$ is Kan by [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Its fiber at $(b,a)$ is the arrow mapping space $U_X(b,a)$, naturally equivalent to $\operatorname{Map}_X(b,a)$ by [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. Along paths $s:b\to b'$ and $h:a\to a'$ its transport is $\beta\mapsto h\beta s^{-1}$: a square in the arrow space says $\beta's=h\beta$, and both paths are invertible in the space $X$. These are the precomposition/postcomposition transports, with their coherent homotopies, of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification]. Hence this arrow space realizes the mapping-space functor with both endpoints allowed to vary, after identifying the contravariant endpoint by inversion. This identification includes all simplicial parameters by the naturality clauses of the pinch comparison and transport classification.

proof.text: For an input list $((a_0,b_1),\ldots,(a_{n-1},b_n))$, the explicit formula of [lem-coef-operad-groupoid-operator-map] gives the active-operation space $G(x,a_0)\times\prod_{i=1}^{n-1}G(b_i,a_i)\times G(b_n,y)$. Its identity-arity source changes are independent unary operations $(r_i:a'_i\to a_i,s_i:b_i\to b'_i)$. Substitution gives the triangle relations $\alpha=r_0\alpha'$, $\beta_i=r_i\beta'_i s_i$ and $\gamma=\gamma's_n$. Put $h_i=r_i^{-1}$. These relations are exactly the coherent endpoint triangles for $A_x$, the internal arrow squares $\beta'_i s_i=h_i\beta_i$, and the endpoint triangles for $B_y$. As in Steps 1 and 3, [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] identifies the enriched factors and their compositions with the coherent mapping-space functor, and [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] identifies their total spaces. Variables in the different factors are disjoint. The product therefore classifies precisely this same functor and gives $\operatorname{Op}_{O,n}(x,y)\simeq A_x\times\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,X)^{n-1}\times B_y$.

proof.text: The formula for $\Phi_G$ in [lem-coef-operad-groupoid-operator-map] sends $(z_0,\ldots,z_n;a:z_0\to x,b:z_n\to y)$ to the list of adjacent pairs with operation $(a^{-1},1_{z_1},\ldots,1_{z_{n-1}},b)$. Thus the endpoint factors in Steps 2 and 4 are unchanged, and each internal coordinate $z_i$ becomes the constant path $1_{z_i}$. A source change $u_i$ becomes $(u_{i-1}^{-1},u_i)$ on the adjacent pair, so in Step 4 its two endpoint changes at the internal constant path are both $u_i$. This is exactly the action of the constant-path map on a varying simplex. The prescribed functor commutes with simplicial operators, and [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] and [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] are natural on these maps. Consequently the identification is of the full induced map of operation spaces, with all higher simplices.

proof.text: Specialize [lem-coef-space-path-fibration-replacement] to $\operatorname{id}_X:X\to X$. Its mapping-path object is $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,X)$, and its constant-path inclusion is exactly $c:X\to\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,X)$, so $c$ is an equivalence. An inverse for the product map of Step 5 is endpoint evaluation on each internal factor, with identities on $A_x$ and $B_y$; the inverse homotopies are the coordinatewise inverse homotopies for $c$. Equivalently these homotopies are given explicitly by $H(\gamma,t)(s)=\gamma(\min(s,t))$, which joins the constant path at $\gamma(0)$ to $\gamma$ and commutes with simplicial operators. Thus the positive-arity map is an equivalence. When $n=1$ the internal product is a point and the map is already the identity on $A_x\times B_y$.

proof.text: For $n=0$ the string source is a single object $z$, and its active mapping space is $G(z,x)\times G(z,y)$ by [lem-coef-simplicial-operator-nerve], since both endpoints of $[1]\to[0]$ select $z$. By [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] and [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], its total space is the space of coherent spans $(z,a:z\to x,b:z\to y)$, with simultaneous source changes and all their homotopies. Normalize such a span by the source equivalence $a:z\to x$, obtaining $(x,1_x,ba^{-1})$. This exhibits a coherent equivalence to the space of arrows $x\to y$, with inverse $h\mapsto(x,1_x,h)$. More explicitly a triangle from $(z,a,b)$ to $(z',a',b')$ has $a'u\simeq a$, $b'u\simeq b$; hence $b'(a')^{-1}\simeq ba^{-1}$. The components $a$ form the equivalence from a span to its normalized span, and the preceding triangle equations are its naturality homotopies. Their higher compatibilities are precisely the coherent composition, unit and transport compatibilities of the two cited comparison/classification nodes; the formulas use the strict simplicial inversion and composition in $G$. Thus this is a comparison of spaces, not merely a bijection of span classes. The arrow mapping space with endpoints fixed is equivalent to $\operatorname{Map}_X(x,y)$ by [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison].

proof.text: On the $O$ side the arity-zero source list is empty, its identity-arity fiber is the terminal space, and its operation space is exactly $G(x,y)$ by the $n=0$ clause of [lem-coef-operad-groupoid-operator-map] and the operator formula of [lem-coef-simplicial-operator-nerve]. Therefore [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] identifies it with $\operatorname{Map}_X(x,y)$. The prescribed zero-length-block formula for $\Phi_G$ sends $(z,a,b)$ to $ba^{-1}$. This is exactly the normalization map of Step 7, whose inverse on the span description is $h\mapsto(x,1_x,h)$. Hence the nullary induced map is an equivalence as well. All changes of source used here stay over the identity of $[0]$, just as those of Steps 2--5 stay over the identity of $[n]$.
